history.dynasty: None (19th century; built by Seth Govind Das and Seth Radha Krishna under the guidance of Sri Rangadeshik Swami)
history.period: Construction 1845-1851; inaugurated 1851; Sri Rangji Trust functioning from 1867
history.summary: The Sri Rangji Temple of Vrindavan - the largest temple in Vrindavan - was built in 1851 (construction 1845-1851) by philanthropists Seth Govind Das and Seth Radha Krishna under Sri Rangadeshik Swami, modelled on the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple at Srirangam, Tamil Nadu. It is unique in Braj for its blend of Dravidian architecture (massive gopuram, inner layout) and North Indian/Rajput stonework (outer gates). The presiding deity, Lord Ranganatha, is depicted as a bridegroom with a walking stick, with Goddess Andal on his right and Garuda on his left - fulfilling the 8th-century saint Andal's desire to marry the Lord. The complex holds a 50-ft gold-plated Dhwaja Stambha and a 50-ft wooden chariot; during the 10-day Brahmotsavam (March-April) the deity is paraded on a 60-ft chariot pulled by thousands of devotees, like Puri's Rath Yatra. The complex also houses shrines to Sudarshana, Narasimha, Venkateswara, Venu Gopala, the Alwars, Ramanujacharya and the founder. Managed by the Sri Rangji Mandir Trust since 1867. NOTE: CSV town 'Mathura' corrected to Vrindavan - the temple stands in Vrindavan, Mathura district, about 14 km from Mathura Junction.

name: Rangji Temple
town_description: Vrindavan is a temple town in Mathura district on the Yamuna, at the heart of the Braj region where Lord Krishna is believed to have spent his childhood. Home to hundreds of temples old and new - Banke Bihari, ISKCON, Prem Mandir - it draws millions of pilgrims each year and lies about 14 km north of Mathura city.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 150 km; Agra Airport about 70 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction, about 14 km; Vrindavan station serves local trains.
travel.road: On Parikrama Marg / Mathura-Vrindavan Road; regular buses and taxis from Delhi and Agra; auto-rickshaws and cycle rickshaws locally.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Brahmotsavam (March-April) is the grandest festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer: 5:30-11:00 AM and 4:00-9:00 PM; winter: 5:30 AM-12:00 PM and 3:00-9:00 PM (per bhaktibharat.com - verify locally). Free entry.
